historical_reviews.deepseek: The selected TEMP_DCSCM label is not established as CPU temperature by this row and may have leaked from the separate duplicate-code sensor variant; truncated output can hide the correct CPU record.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires a vendor CPU-to-sensor locator map and complete read-only evidence before evaluating correctness.
historical_reviews.history: The shared code also identifies row 1833 named TEMP_DCSCM; source row and variant ID prevent that separate identity from silently defining row 1651.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Sensor correctness requires entity provenance, not a name substring. `CPU` may match non-temperature or aggregate records, while `TEMP_DCSCM` may measure a management module rather than a CPU. The platform map must link each CPU socket to the exact sensor/entity before any range judgment.

original_test_intent: Read the platform's CPU temperature sensor data through in-band IPMI and verify that every required CPU/socket reading is present, readable, correctly identified and within the approved unit/status/range policy.
original_method: Verify the exact duplicate-code variant, map CPU sockets to approved sensor records, capture complete protected in-band sensor/SDR evidence with entity, units, status, thresholds and timestamp, compare values to platform rules and a same-target authoritative source, and preserve all logs without mutation.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor supplies the socket-to-sensor map and expected semantics; an operator verifies the target and reviews any mismatch between IPMI and the authoritative platform or structured view.
required_inputs: Expected unit, status, range and threshold policy
safety_requirements: Do not assume TEMP_DCSCM or first CPU match
Reject stale, duplicate, malformed or unitless values
Stop on target or mapping mismatch
Never alter thresholds or fans to force a reading
agent_execution_scope: Parse values, units, status, thresholds and freshness

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sensor get TEMP_DCSCM` is not justified as CPU temperature for this variant; unsafe SSH and a 100-line fallback can omit the intended record and do not define correctness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the complete protected in-band IPMI sensor/SDR query, select only owner-approved CPU sensor IDs after retaining raw output, and compare full entity/value/unit/status/threshold/freshness fields with the approved mapping and same-target source.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The in-band IPMI path and 5/5-minute read-only check remain; the incomplete source `Check` is made measurable without importing row 1833's TEMP_DCSCM identity.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Produce a per-socket ledger containing physical socket, sensor ID/entity, raw and normalized value, unit, status, thresholds, timestamp/freshness and authoritative cross-check.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces substring filtering and a guessed DCSCM sensor with platform-bound record identity and complete evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One readable temperature cannot prove all installed CPU sockets are represented or that the sensor actually measures a CPU.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Different firmware may expose package, die, control or margin temperatures with different semantics; normalization requires vendor definitions rather than generic Celsius bounds.

project_override_considerations: The Project must keep this AMD CPU Management variant separate from row 1833's TEMP_DCSCM sensor-list case and explicitly state whether DCSCM is ever authoritative for CPU temperature on this platform.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant, target identity and CPU topology

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: This exact row consistently requests CPU temperature through in-band IPMI. Its incomplete `Check` and missing sensor mapping are prerequisite gaps; the distinct row-1833 duplicate variant is isolated rather than merged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A vendor sensor map and policy can normally resolve the target and acceptance rules. Execution blocks only if exact CPU sensor identity or protected read access cannot be established.

review_improvement: Prevents a management-module temperature guessed from another duplicate-code row from being reported as CPU temperature and requires complete socket coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Sensor labels are firmware-defined and not guaranteed to encode physical ownership. A CPU-named grep can include power rails or status flags, while a DCSCM temperature can be physically unrelated. Entity/locator mapping and topology completeness are necessary before range checks, and freshness must be verified because stale but plausible values can survive a failed sensor path.
